title: Akhbar al-Adhkiya' (Kitab al-Adhkiya')
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0597IbnJawzi.Adhkiya.JK000910-ara1; base print edition: Maktabat al-Ghazali (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 597 AH / 1201 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Anthology of anecdotes on intelligence in 33 chapters (author's own table of contents): chapters on judges (12), rulers/governors/police (11), Arabs (15), thieves (28), clever children (29) and women (31) hold most inference stories.

Contains verified versions of: the sons of Nizar inferring a lost camel's traits from grazing, tracks and dung (ch.15, p.84-85); the Wasit judge exposing a swapped deposit by the mint dates on coins (ch.12, p.64-65); Iyas's 'has your adversary reached the tree yet?' test (p.65); Adud al-Dawla tracing money buried under a castor-oil plant via physicians' prescriptions (ch.11, p.51-52).
States three purposes: knowing the clever, sharpening the listener's mind, and humbling the self-satisfied (preface).
athar_applications: Primary wellspring for ATHAR heritage micro-cases; most anecdotes are non-violent property disputes (deposits, thefts) suitable for 13-15.
Stored internally (OPEN_LICENSE folder) for retrieval of exact wording by writers; retell in our own words.
limitations: Anecdote collection with isnads of uneven reliability; attributions are often legendary.
Some stories embed slavery, gender norms, corporal punishment or coerced confession and need rewriting.
OpenITI file is a 'cleaned' digital text without critical apparatus; page refs follow OpenITI's PageV markers.

title: al-Turuq al-hukmiyya fi al-siyasa al-shar'iyya
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0751IbnQayyimJawziyya.TuruqHukmiyya.JK000104-ara1; base print edition: ed. Muhammad Jamil Ghazi, Cairo: Matba'at al-Madani (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 751 AH / 1350 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Opens by asking whether a judge may rule by firasa: neglecting signs loses rights, but relying on them instead of legal proofs causes injustice (p.3).
Distinguishes two kinds of understanding a judge needs: of general rules, and of the facts and people's circumstances (fiqh al-waqi') (p.4).

Collects firasa anecdotes (Iyas, Shurayh, Ka'b ibn Sur, Abu Hazim, Ibn Tulun, al-Mu'tadid) and states that jurists require separating suspect witnesses and asking how and where they witnessed (p.33-34).
Treats qafa (lineage/foot reading) as a legal path, citing Mujazziz al-Mudliji and trackers sent after the 'Uraniyyun (p.314-316).
athar_applications: Main doctrinal source for ATHAR's heritage framing: 'signs of the situation' (shawahid al-hal) map onto circumstantial evidence and abductive inference.
Its own warning against over-reliance on signs gives ATHAR an indigenous argument for 'insight is not evidence' (Atlas principle 46).
limitations: Normative juristic text with a Hanbali reform agenda; anecdotes are illustrative, not case records.
Endorses practices incompatible with modern rights (beating suspects, coerced confession used to find stolen goods, p.10-11; punishments).
The OpenITI file contains inline variant readings in triple brackets.

title: Akhbar al-qudat
authors: Waki', Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Hayyan
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0306Wakic.AkhbarQudat.JK007001-ara1; base print edition: Beirut: 'Alam al-Kutub (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 306 AH / 918 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Earliest large biographical collection on judges by city; the Basra section has dozens of Iyas entries with headings such as 'Firasat Iyas', 'Iyas's ruse to recover a deposit', and the two-cloaks case (p.326-341).
Gives isnad-bearing versions of stories later reused by Ibn al-Jawzi and Ibn Qayyim (e.g., the red/green cloaks and the comb, p.337-338; the tree question, p.341).
athar_applications: Earliest attestation layer for Iyas stories; lets ATHAR show story migration across centuries (a teaching point on sources).
limitations: OpenITI flags RANDOM_CHARS and MISSING_PARTS in this version; editorial section headings are OpenITI/edition additions.

title: Nishwar al-muhadara wa-akhbar al-mudhakara
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0384MuhassinTanukhi.NishwarMuhadara.Shamela0010275BK1-ara1; base print edition: Shamela 10275, 8 vols (ed. 'Abbud al-Shalji, per WorldCat link in OpenITI metadata)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 384 AH / 994 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Numbered anecdotes from 4th/10th-century Baghdad: a governor of Egypt doubts a forged vizieral letter because its praise and tone exceed the bearer's standing (no.21, vol.1 p.56-59).

Qadi Abu 'Umar refuses a witness who performed exaggerated disgust at the smell of spilled wine (no.89, vol.2 p.170); a Hamadan judge rejects a witness whose step count changed (no.130, vol.1 p.245); a dog leads to its master's killers (no.180, vol.1 p.339).
athar_applications: Rich source for document-forgery and witness-credibility micro-cases set in an urban bureaucracy (offices, letters, seals).
limitations: This OpenITI version retains modern editor footnote markers and some note lines; therefore NOT stored, link only.
Eyewitness 'I was told' chains; entertainment literature.

title: al-Faraj ba'd al-shidda
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0384MuhassinTanukhi.FarajBacdaShidda.Shamela0012828-ara1; base print edition: ed. 'Abbud al-Shalji, Beirut: Dar Sadir 1398/1978 (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 384 AH / 994 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Thematic collection of deliverance stories; includes ruses and documentary manipulation in the Abbasid administration (e.g., a tax-bureau head intercepting a caliphal order, p.388).
athar_applications: Secondary pool for 'escape the frame-up' and 'clear your name' arcs.
limitations: Fewer pure inference stories than Akhbar al-Adhkiya'; many tales hinge on prayer, chance or patronage (violates fair-play).

title: Kalila wa-Dimna (incl. 'Bab al-fahs 'an amr Dimna')
title_ar: كليلة ودمنة (ومنه باب الفحص عن أمر دمنة)
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0139IbnMuqaffac.KalilaWaDimna.Shamela0026537-ara1; base print edition: Cairo: al-Matba'a al-Amiriyya bi-Bulaq, 17th printing 1355 AH / 1936-37
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. c. 139-142 AH / c. 757-759 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: The chapter 'Investigation of Dimna's case' (p.153-175 in this version) is a full inquiry: an overheard confession, a secret informant, a judge (the leopard) holding open sessions, rhetorical defence, and conviction only once a second witness joins the first because one testimony cannot decide a case (p.173).
Within the trial, Dimna ridicules a physiognomic accusation based on an asymmetric eye and crooked nose (p.~167).

Other chapters model reasoning errors: the ascetic who kills his loyal weasel by jumping to conclusions (p.239) and the ascetic jackal framed with planted meat whose case is reopened by the lion's mother (p.266-270).
athar_applications: Ready-made templates for a 'trial' episode, a frame-up case, and a 'don't jump to conclusions' tutorial with animal characters (safe distance for 13-15).
limitations: Ibn al-Muqaffa's original is lost; versions differ most in the Dimna chapter (see ATH-SRC-1231); this is a late Bulaq vulgate.
The Dimna chapter ends in an execution and frames justice as reason of state.

title: Akhbar al-hamqa wa-l-mughaffalin
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0597IbnJawzi.AkhbarHamqaWaMughaffalin.JK000004-ara1; base print edition: Beirut: al-Maktab al-Tijari (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 597 AH / 1201 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Companion to Akhbar al-Adhkiya' collecting failures of judgement: a man marks buried money by a cloud (Juha section, p.46); a gullible judge skips Friday prayer because a stranger says it was postponed (judges chapter 13, p.101); a complainant who can describe the wrongdoer only by a 'mole or slap mark or burn' and 'a name with ta' or lam' (ch.24, p.175).
athar_applications: Error library for ATHAR: each anecdote is a named reasoning failure (unstable reference point, unverified claim, uninformative description).
limitations: Humour depends partly on mocking disability and social groups; select carefully.

title: Nihayat al-rutba fi talab al-hisba
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0590IbnNasrJalalDinShayzari.NihayatRutba.Shamela0021584-ara1; base print edition: Cairo: Matba'at Lajnat al-Ta'lif wa-l-Tarjama wa-l-Nashr (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. c. 590 AH / 1193 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Forty chapters assigning the market inspector checks per trade; ch.4 explains how a true balance is built and lists hidden weighing tricks (oil residue on pans, hand pressure, blowing on the pan) (p.17-18).

Ch.17 (pharmacists) pairs each adulteration with a detection test, e.g., tabashir mixed with burnt bone separates in water (bone sinks), and resin-adulterated frankincense betrays itself when burned (p.42-44).
athar_applications: Template for 'market inspector' micro-cases built on simple physical tests (density, burning, appearance) simulated safely in-app.
limitations: Some tests involve tasting or burning substances: simulate only; never instruct players to taste unknowns.
Lists adulteration methods; ATHAR should show detection, not recipes (protocol safety rule).

title: Kitab al-Manazir, Books I-III (Arabic text)
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0430IbnHaytham.Manazir.ALCorpus00006-ara2; base print edition: transcription (Azzam Hasan, Kaddour Alkassem; Arabic and Latin Corpus, Univ. of Wurzburg) of A. I. Sabra's edition (Kuwait, 1983)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. c. 430 AH / c. 1040 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Book I ch.2 uses repeated controlled trials with a tube: when the tube is blocked the object is not seen, establishing that vision occurs only along straight lines; the text calls the procedure i'tibar and pairs it with induction (istiqra') (paras 9-21, p.65-68).
athar_applications: Basis for a 'test, don't trust' lab mechanic (block the line, observe, repeat) and for ATHAR's methodological motto.
limitations: Do not claim he 'invented the scientific method' (contested; see ATH-SRC-0731, ATH-SRC-1243).
The transcription follows a modern critical edition; the Wurzburg page displays CC BY-SA 4.0 and OpenITI redistributes under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 - the stricter NC terms are applied here.

title: Kitab al-Hayawan
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0255Jahiz.Hayawan.Shamela0023775-ara1; base print edition: Beirut: Dar al-Kutub al-'Ilmiyya (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 255 AH / 869 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Reports al-Jahiz's own replication of a claim about dung beetles on a darkling beetle (no.798, vol.3 p.165).
Describes hares stepping on their hairy foot-pads so that dogs and trackers (qa'if) cannot read their prints, and gazelles entering their lair backwards (no.1699, vol.6 p.338).
Mentions famous lineage-readers Mujazziz al-Mudliji and Ibn Kurayz al-Khuza'i as benchmarks of qiyafa (no.85, vol.1 p.81-82).
athar_applications: Observation-and-replication voice for an in-world naturalist character; anti-tracking animal behaviours make good 'counter-trace' puzzles.
limitations: This OpenITI version retains editor footnote markers and note lines; NOT stored, link only.
Mixes observation with hearsay; not reliable natural history.

title: Subh al-a'sha fi sina'at al-insha'
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0821Qalqashandi.SubhAcsha.Shamela0009429-ara1; base print edition: Beirut: Dar al-Kutub al-'Ilmiyya (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 821 AH / 1418 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Reports that Harun al-Rashid ordered official writing on paper rather than skins because skins allow erasure and rewriting (forgery), whereas paper is spoiled by erasure and scraping shows (vol.2 p.514-515).
athar_applications: Anchor for document cases: the medium itself as an anti-forgery control; erasure traces as evidence.
limitations: Encyclopaedic chancery manual (14 vols); only targeted passages verified this session; the attribution to Harun is a report, not a dated decree.

title: Kashf al-zunun 'an asami al-kutub wa-l-funun
title_ar: كشف الظنون عن أسامي الكتب والفنون
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 1067HajjiKhalifa.KashfZunun.JK000468-ara1; base print edition: Beirut: Dar al-Kutub al-'Ilmiyya 1413/1992 (OpenITI ed_info)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 1067 AH / 1657 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Defines 'ilm al-'iyafa as following the traces of feet, hooves and pads on ground that holds prints, useful for finding fugitives and strays, and notes as 'strange' claims to tell a young from an old foot or a man's from a woman's (vol.2 p.1180).

Splits qiyafa into qiyafat al-athar (= 'iyafa) and qiyafat al-bashar (lineage from bodily resemblance), says the latter is achieved by conjecture (hads wa-takhmin) not by certain proof, and lists both as branches of firasa (vol.2 p.1365; vol.0 p.14).
athar_applications: Gives ATHAR an authoritative classical definition of qiyafat al-athar for the brand story, plus a classical admission that lineage-reading is conjectural.
limitations: Late bibliographic encyclopaedia; definitions summarise earlier taxonomies (e.g., Tashkopruzade) rather than practice.

title: OpenITI: a Machine-Readable Corpus of Islamicate Texts (release 2025.1.9)
key_findings: Zenodo lists the release licence as CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the KITAB documentation repeats this and says editorial input of in-copyright editions (footnotes, introductions) must be removed during annotation.
Most texts were scraped from open digital libraries (Shamela is the largest); metadata file records base print edition and quality tags (e.g., NO_MAJOR_ISSUES, MISSING_PARTS).
athar_applications: Legal basis for storing premodern Arabic texts internally (non-commercial research). Any commercial ATHAR text must be our own retelling or re-keyed from a public-domain print, not the OpenITI file.
limitations: Some Shamela-derived versions still contain editor footnote markers (observed in Nishwar and Hayawan); check per file before storing.
NC licence: no commercial reuse of the digital files.

title: Alf layla wa-layla (Hindawi digital edition, OpenITI version)
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying anonymous premodern text public domain; Hindawi's terms for this digital edition not verified
key_findings: The tale of the girl, the apples and the slave Rayhan (the 'Three Apples') begins in night 19 (heading after p.18) and the Hunchback cycle at night 24-25, running past night 34, in this night-numbered text.
The Hunchback cycle is a chain in which four people each believe they caused the death and each confesses to save the next accused.
athar_applications: Arabic reference text for the two most-cited 'crime' frames in the Nights; retell, never copy.
limitations: Not stored: Hindawi licence for this digital edition not established in-session.
Contains violence against women, slavery and racialised depictions; vulgate, not the oldest manuscript layer.

title: The Arabian Nights Entertainments (selected and edited by Andrew Lang)
rights_jurisdiction: US (published 1898); UK/EU life+70 expired (Lang d. 1912); Arab states life+50 expired
key_findings: Contains 'The Story of Ali Colia, Merchant of Bagdad' (Ali Cogia): a deposit of gold hidden under olives is stolen and the olives replaced; children playing at being the cadi expose the theft by asking olive merchants whether seven-year-old olives could look fresh.
Contains 'The Little Hunchback' chain of mistaken guilt (tailor, doctor, purveyor, broker).
athar_applications: Public-domain English text of the child-judge story, the clearest heritage model for a teen investigator and for expert testimony against a time anomaly.
limitations: Lang's selection is bowdlerised for children and derives from Galland's French, not Arabic manuscripts.
Keep the PG header if redistributed under the PG name (trademark; see ATH-SRC-1024).

title: Book of Charlatans (Kitab al-Mukhtar fi kashf al-asrar)
publisher: New York University Press (Library of Arabic Literature)
key_findings: 13th-century Damascene exposé of fraudsters' tricks, organised in 30 chapters; the OpenITI metadata reproduces the LAL editorial declaration (base manuscripts, variants, the concealment jargon al-Sin).
athar_applications: Background for 'debunk the charlatan' cases (fake miracle-workers, false alchemists) at the level of red flags only.
limitations: Describes fraud techniques in detail: use only for detection cues, never as method (protocol safety).
Modern critical edition and translation are copyrighted; not stored.

title: The Classical Arabic Detective
key_findings: Peer-reviewed study (Arabica 35(1):59-91) treating the detective figure in classical Arabic adab anecdotes as a literary type; reprinted 2022 in her collected studies (Routledge, Power, Marginality, and the Body in Medieval Islam).
athar_applications: Scholarly warrant for presenting the heritage anecdotes as a native 'detective' tradition rather than as an anachronistic label.
limitations: Full text not read this session (paywalled); content claims beyond title/venue must be checked before citing specifics.

title: Classical Arabic Crime Narratives: Thieves and Thievery in Adab Literature
key_findings: Peer-reviewed article (JAL 19(2):108-127) on thief anecdotes as a crime-narrative genre in adab collections.
athar_applications: Background for the thieves' chapter of Akhbar al-Adhkiya' (ch.28) and for 'inverted' heritage cases told from the culprit's ruse.
limitations: Full text not read this session.

title: Signs as Evidence: The Doctrine of Ibn Taymiyya (1263-1328) and Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya (d. 1351) on Proof
key_findings: Peer-reviewed analysis (ILS 9(2):168-193) of how Ibn Taymiyya and Ibn Qayyim expanded admissible proof to 'signs' (amarat/qara'in) beyond testimony and confession.
athar_applications: Academic anchor for ATHAR's claim that classical Islamic law debated circumstantial evidence explicitly; frames HER principles on signs vs. testimony.
limitations: Full text not read; specific doctrinal claims in our overview rely on the primary text ATH-SRC-1201.

title: Firasah as a Basic Condition for Achieving Justice in the Judiciary: An Appraisal of the Views of Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah
publisher: Islamic Research Institute, International Islamic University Islamabad (Islamic Studies 63:4)
key_findings: Abstract: Ibn Qayyim held that judges should use indications and circumstantial evidence besides confession and testimony, with outcomes depending on the judge's acuity and the clarity of evidence.
Abstract: he rejected Greek physiognomy, and most jurists disagreed with his broad approach.
athar_applications: Shows the classical debate itself was contested: useful for ATHAR's 'debate the method' tasks.
limitations: Abstract-level verification only; pages 489-506.

title: The Expert Witness in Islamic Courts: Medicine and Crafts in the Service of Law
key_findings: Examines physicians, architects, midwives and other experts as witnesses in Islamic legal systems that favoured eyewitness testimony, through Egypt's reforms from the late 19th century.
Chapter 6 'From Physiognomy to DNA Testing' (pp.154-188) traces paternity proof from qiyafa to DNA.
athar_applications: Bridge from classical qa'if (lineage reader) to modern forensic expertise; supports an ATHAR lesson on how evidence standards change.
limitations: Chapter content verified at title level only.

title: Islamic Law of Paternity Between Classical Legal Texts and Modern Contexts: From Physiognomy to DNA Analysis
publisher: Oxford University Press (Journal of Islamic Studies 25:1)
key_findings: Peer-reviewed article (JIS 25(1):1-32) on how classical rules on qiyafa are invoked in modern debates on DNA paternity testing.
athar_applications: Second scholarly anchor for the qiyafa-to-forensics bridge; flags that lineage topics are sensitive.
limitations: Full text not read; lineage/paternity is unsuitable as an ATHAR case topic for teens.

title: Origins of Cryptology: The Arab Contributions
key_findings: Peer-reviewed survey (Cryptologia 16(2):97-126, April 1992) of Arabic cryptology manuscripts, including al-Kindi's treatise on decipherment and later works by Ibn 'Adlan and Ibn al-Durayhim.
athar_applications: Source for a code-breaking heritage strand: frequency counting as an evidence-based inference skill.
limitations: Crossref lists the author surname as 'Al-Kadit' (metadata typo).

title: Series on Arabic Origins of Cryptology (vol. 1: al-Kindi's Treatise on Cryptanalysis)
publisher: King Faisal Center for Research and Islamic Studies & KACST
key_findings: English edition and translation series of Arabic cryptology manuscripts found largely in Istanbul (Suleymaniye) by a Damascus team from 1979; published in Arabic 1987 (per ATH-SRC-1224).
athar_applications: Authoritative edition to cite for al-Kindi's frequency-analysis method in an ATHAR cipher episode.
limitations: Catalog record only; volume count and per-volume dates need a library check.

title: Arab Origins of Cryptology
key_findings: Names al-Kindi's 'Risala fi istikhraj al-mu'amma' (c. 850 CE) as the oldest extant cryptologic text and credits it with letter-frequency analysis of substitution ciphers.
Reports the 1979 Damascus search (Mrayati, Alam, al-Tayyan) that recovered Ibn al-Durayhim's 'Miftah al-kunuz fi idah al-marmuz' and 15+ other manuscripts, mostly in Istanbul.
athar_applications: Accessible overview for writers; cite ATH-SRC-1222/1223 for claims.
limitations: Heritage-promotion site; not peer reviewed; some claims ('oldest') should be phrased cautiously.

title: An Account of Early Statistical Inference in Arab Cryptology
key_findings: Short peer-reviewed note (pp.255-257) presenting Arab cryptanalysis as an early use of statistical reasoning (letter frequencies).
athar_applications: Supports framing frequency analysis as 'base-rate' reasoning in ATHAR's cipher strand.
limitations: Full text not read.

title: Story-Telling Techniques in the Arabian Nights
key_findings: Monograph on narrative devices of the Nights; already cited via ATH-SRC-0139 for successive-revelation suspense in the Three Apples.
athar_applications: Reference for adapting Nights frame structures (nested confessions, deadline frame).
limitations: Not read in full this session.

title: The Arabian Nights Encyclopedia
key_findings: Two-volume standard reference with entries on individual tales and their versions.
athar_applications: Check source layer of any Nights tale before ATHAR claims it is 'Arabic heritage' (some famous tales are Galland-era additions).
limitations: Not consulted entry-by-entry this session.

title: The Man Who Made the Nights Immortal: The Tales of the Syrian Maronite Storyteller Hanna Diyab
key_findings: Lists 16 tales the Aleppine Hanna Diyab told Antoine Galland in 1709; 'Ali Khawaja and the Merchant of Baghdad' was told on 29 May 1709 (tale type 1617, unjust banker).
Notes the olive-swap detail is otherwise known only from recent oral tradition; the article is internally inconsistent on whether Galland published this tale.
athar_applications: Correct provenance label for the child-judge story: an 18th-century Syrian oral tale recorded in French, not a medieval Arabic manuscript tale.
limitations: Author-hosted PDF; publication rights belong to the journal.

title: The Story of the 'Orphan Tales' in the Arabian Nights between Antoine Galland and Hanna Diyab
publisher: Damascus University Journal of Arts and Humanities Sciences 36:3
key_findings: Arabic-language scholarship arguing from Galland's diaries and Diyab's travel memoir that Diyab authored the 'orphan tales' (no known written Arabic source).
athar_applications: Arabic citation for ATHAR's provenance notes on Galland-era tales.
limitations: Abstract-level verification.

title: Marvellous Thieves: Secret Authors of the Arabian Nights
key_findings: Monograph on the collaborators (including Hanna Diyab) behind European editions of the Nights.
athar_applications: Further reading on provenance.
limitations: Not read this session.

title: Versions of 'Dimna's Trial' in Kalila and Dimna as a spectrum of legal and ethical positions (AOS 2024 talk)
publisher: Freie Universitat Berlin, Kalila and Dimna project (event page)
key_findings: Talk abstract (AOS, Chicago, 22 March 2024): Ibn al-Muqaffa' added the trial as a sequel to 'The Lion and the Ox'; the verdict is pre-set by reason of state (the lion's mother), yet Dimna makes the strongest legal arguments on proof, judicial ethics and false confession.
The court moves between physiognomy (firasa) and testimony (shahada); this chapter varies more than any other across manuscripts, some with mutually exclusive plots.
athar_applications: Strong design hook: a trial whose 'winner' argues best but is still guilty - teaches separating rhetoric from evidence.
limitations: Event abstract, not a publication; cite with the project's peer-reviewed volumes (ATH-SRC-1232).

title: Dimna's Trial and Apologia in Kashifi's Anvar-i Suhayli: Morality's Place in the Corrupt Trial of a Rhetorical and Dialectical Genius
publisher: Cambridge University Press (Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 26:4)
key_findings: Peer-reviewed study (JRAS 26(4):549-583) reading the trial as corrupt and Dimna as a rhetorical-dialectical genius in the Persian reworking.
athar_applications: Confirms the trial's ambiguity is a scholarly theme, supporting an ATHAR 'argument vs evidence' episode.
limitations: Concerns the Persian Anvar-i Suhayli version, not the Arabic vulgate.

title: The Book of the Islamic Market Inspector: Nihayat al-Rutba fi Talab al-Hisba
publisher: Oxford University Press (Journal of Semitic Studies Supplement 9)
key_findings: Annotated English translation of al-Shayzari's hisba manual (ATH-SRC-1207).
athar_applications: English reference for non-Arabic-reading team members and for terminology.
limitations: Series detail recalled, not seen on the catalog page: verify 'JSS Supplement 9' before print.

title: Islamic Law in Action: Authority, Discretion, and Everyday Experiences in Mamluk Egypt
key_findings: Monograph on how Mamluk-era muhtasibs actually exercised discretion, from chronicles rather than manuals.
athar_applications: Corrective to idealised hisba manuals: practice involved discretion, coercion and politics.
limitations: Not read this session; Crossref online date 2012, print 2011.

title: Justice, Punishment and the Medieval Muslim Imagination
key_findings: Monograph on punishment and its representation in medieval Islamic societies (chapter 'Types of punishment', pp.61-98).
athar_applications: Context for ATHAR's rule to strip premodern punishments from adaptations.
limitations: Not read this session.

title: Doubt in Islamic Law: A History of Legal Maxims, Interpretation, and Islamic Criminal Law
key_findings: Monograph on the maxim to avert fixed punishments in cases of doubt (shubha) and its interpretive history; reviewed in Islamic Law and Society 24(3), 2017.
athar_applications: Indigenous counterpart to 'reasonable doubt': ATHAR can teach that the tradition itself counselled caution when evidence is doubtful.
limitations: Crossref lists a placeholder year (1920); publication 2015 per Cambridge (verify).

title: In Quest of Justice: Islamic Law and Forensic Medicine in Modern Egypt
key_findings: Monograph on how 19th-century Egyptian courts integrated forensic medicine and documentary evidence alongside sharia.
athar_applications: Shows the historical bridge from qara'in to modern forensic evidence in an Arab country.
limitations: Not read this session.

title: Qadis Communicating: Legal Change and the Law of Documentary Evidence
key_findings: Peer-reviewed article on how Islamic law came to accept written judicial communications as evidence despite a doctrinal preference for oral testimony.
athar_applications: Background for document-authentication cases (seals, letters, witnesses to writing).
limitations: Not read this session.

title: Firasa and Intelligence: The Silly and the Intelligent in Arab Physiognomy
publisher: ELTE (The Arabist: Budapest Studies in Arabic 17)
key_findings: Study (pp.121-131) of how Arabic physiognomic treatises link bodily signs to intelligence and folly.
athar_applications: Evidence that 'physiognomic' firasa claimed to read character from the body - the strand ATHAR must flag as pseudoscience.
limitations: Not read in full.

AUDIT-W2 2026-10-27: legal_text_access paywalled -> free_official: the journal page (arabist.hu, volume 17) offers a direct 'Download PDF' (HTTP 200, application/pdf) without login. No open licence is stated, so rights stay COPYRIGHTED_RESTRICTED and nothing was stored.

title: Firasa (Encyclopaedia of Islam, Second Edition)
key_findings: Standard reference entry on firasa (physiognomy and intuitive discernment); DOI confirmed via Crossref.
athar_applications: Reference definition for the glossary.
limitations: Author and content not verified (Brill page refused fetch).

title: Kiyafa (Encyclopaedia of Islam, Second Edition)
key_findings: Standard reference entry on qiyafa (tracking and lineage-reading); DOI confirmed via Crossref.
athar_applications: Reference anchor for the brand-name discussion (qiyafat al-athar).
limitations: Author and content not verified (Brill page refused fetch).

title: The science of Arabic Physiognomy since the Pre-Islamic until the Prophet and caliphs era
publisher: Tishreen University Journal, Arts and Humanities Sciences Series 39:1
key_findings: Abstract: Arabs developed reading footprints in sand to identify people, animals and horses; the practice was endorsed in early Islam and used for lineage, with companions differing on its probative reach.
athar_applications: Arabic-university source on qiyafa history for Arabic-language brand copy.
limitations: Abstract-level; Syrian university journal, editorial standards unknown.

title: Ibn al-Haytham (Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers)
key_findings: Describes al-Shukuk 'ala Batlamyus as a detailed critique of Ptolemy's Almagest, Planetary Hypotheses and Optics, showing where Ptolemy violated principles of natural philosophy (pp.556-557).
Calls him one of the most influential figures in the history of science without claiming he founded the scientific method.
athar_applications: Grounds the 'doubt the authority' strand (al-Shukuk) with a careful, non-hyped source.
limitations: Short entry; does not cover i'tibar.

title: The Optics of Ibn al-Haytham, Books I-III: On Direct Vision (tr. A. I. Sabra) - reviews
publisher: Warburg Institute (1989); reviewed in Isis 82:4 (1991) and Speculum 67:4 (1992)
key_findings: Standard English translation of Kitab al-Manazir I-III, reviewed in Isis (82(4):724-726) and Speculum (67(4):977-980).
athar_applications: English reference for the experiment passages (ATH-SRC-1208).
limitations: Publisher/year of translation recalled (Warburg 1989), not seen in this session - verify.

title: Face Value: The Irresistible Influence of First Impressions
key_findings: Psychology monograph showing people form rapid, consistent trait judgements from faces that are largely inaccurate; traces modern 'scientific' physiognomy's failures.
athar_applications: Modern evidence for ATHAR's rule that face-based firasa is a bias to be debunked, not a skill to be taught.
limitations: Catalog-level verification (Wellcome, Project MUSE).

title: On the Method of Zadig (in Science and Hebrew Tradition)
rights_jurisdiction: US (pub. 1880); UK/EU life+70 expired (Huxley d. 1895); life+50 expired
key_findings: Huxley's 1880 essay uses Voltaire's Zadig (who infers an unseen horse and dog from tracks) to name 'retrospective prophecy' - inferring past causes from present effects - as the method of geology, palaeontology and detection.
athar_applications: Bridges the Arab lost-camel motif to Western philosophy of historical sciences; useful in the heritage overview.
limitations: Duplicate of W2-WORLDLIT ATH-SRC-1330 (same essay, PG #2627); merge should keep ATH-SRC-1330 as canonical. Text already stored by W2-WORLDLIT at 99_LEGAL_SOURCE_ASSETS/PUBLIC_DOMAIN_VERIFIED/huxley_on_the_method_of_zadig/ (TXT-W-032).

title: The Three Princes of Serendip (Wikipedia, bibliographic)
key_findings: The lost-camel episode (one-eyed, lame, carrying honey and butter) appears in Amir Khusrau's Hasht Bihisht (1302) and in Cristoforo Armeno's Italian Peregrinaggio (Venice, 1557); Voltaire adapted it in Zadig ch.3 (1747).
Page cites an earlier Talmudic version but does not mention the Arabic 'sons of Nizar' version.
athar_applications: Shows the Arabic sons-of-Nizar story (ATH-SRC-1200 ch.15) belongs to a wide Eurasian motif - avoid claiming exclusive Arab origin.
limitations: Wikipedia: bibliographic facts only.

title: Ma'alim al-qurba fi talab al-hisba
authors: Ibn al-Ukhuwwa, Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi
publisher: Open Islamicate Texts Initiative (OpenITI) digital edition
edition_version: OpenITI version 0729IbnUkhuwwa.MacalimQurba.JK011677-ara1; base print edition: no print named in primary version; a secondary OpenITI version cites the Cambridge 'Dar al-Funun' print
rights_jurisdiction: Underlying premodern text public domain worldwide (author d. 729 AH / 1329 CE); licence below covers OpenITI's digital file
license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (OpenITI release licence; applies to the digital file only)
key_findings: Chapter 25 (perfumers and candle-makers, p.151-152) repeats al-Shayzari's tests almost word for word: burnt bone in tabashir sinks in water, resin in frankincense flares and smells when burned.
Separate chapter on money-changers (ch.36, p.181) and long sections on coinage and its history.
athar_applications: Text-reuse example for an ATHAR 'source criticism' task: two 'independent' manuals that are actually one source copied.
limitations: Same safety limits as ATH-SRC-1207.

title: Training course on footprint tracking (qass al-athar) for Saudi Border Guards personnel at Naif Arab University for Security Sciences
title_ar: دورة تدريبية عن «قص الأثر» لمنسوبي حرس الحدود
key_findings: Naif Arab University's College of Training ran a footprint-tracking course in Riyadh at the request of the Saudi Border Guards (9-20 Sha'ban; article dated 1 May 2009).
Curriculum covered footprint recognition, trail following, direction of movement, terrain and weather effects, photographic documentation and comparison, and the Robbins scale for foot anatomy.
athar_applications: Evidence that qiyafat al-athar survives as an institutional skill in the Gulf, linking the brand heritage to contemporary practice; ideas for a safe 'read the sand' training level.
limitations: Newspaper report; no evaluation of tracker accuracy. Robbins-scale claims (stature/sex from prints) need forensic-library review before use.

title: Arabic and Latin Corpus: Ibn al-Haytham, Kitab al-Manazir (Arabic text page)
authors: Arabic and Latin Glossary project, University of Wurzburg
key_findings: Page credits the transcription to Azzam Hasan and Kaddour Alkassem, based on A. I. Sabra's edition (Kuwait 1983) plus MSS Istanbul Suleymaniye Fatih 3212-3214, and displays a CC BY-SA 4.0 badge.
athar_applications: Upstream licence for TXT-H-008; if ATHAR ever needs commercial reuse, CC BY-SA from the original host may be preferable to OpenITI's NC copy (lawyer to confirm Sabra-edition rights).
limitations: Badge without written terms; edition rights of Sabra's text (Kuwait 1983) not assessed.

title: Kalila and Dimna; or, The Fables of Bidpai (translated from the Arabic by Wyndham Knatchbull)
publisher: Oxford: W. Baxter for J. Parker
edition_version: Internet Archive bub_gb_Mx4W0HHMJAYC (Google scan of Harvard copy); translated from de Sacy's Arabic edition (Paris 1816)
rights_jurisdiction: US (pub. 1819); UK/EU life+70 expired (translator d. 1868); Arab life+50 expired
key_findings: Table of contents lists chapter VI 'Investigation of the conduct ... of Dimna' after 'The Lion and the Bull'; the chapter opens (book p.160-161) with the leopard overhearing Kalila reproach Dimna.
Preface states the translation follows Silvestre de Sacy's 1816 Arabic text, collated from several manuscripts.
athar_applications: Public-domain English text of the Dimna trial for non-Arabic team members; safe base for any commercial English paraphrase.
limitations: Uncorrected OCR; de Sacy's text is a 19th-century composite edition, not the lost original.

title: Non-canonical Arabic Detective Fiction: The Beginnings of the Genre
publisher: University of Oslo (Journal of Arabic and Islamic Studies 18)
key_findings: Abstract: Arabic detective fiction began with translations in the late 19th/early 20th century and became original Arabic writing in the early 1960s (Egypt-focused); canonical detective novels appeared only from the early 1980s.
Abstract does not discuss premodern precursors (adab, firasa, Nights).
athar_applications: Counterweight to heritage hype: the modern genre came via translation; ATHAR's heritage strand is a precursor tradition of inference, not an unbroken genre lineage.
limitations: Abstract-level verification (pp.23-49).

title: On Arabic Crime Fiction
key_findings: Popular essay (13 Oct 2020) tracing crime narrative to the Three Apples and to anecdotes in Kitab al-Adhkiya', al-Faraj ba'd al-shidda and Kitab al-Aghani, and presenting the Abbasid police chief and al-Mu'tadid ('the case of the painted hand') as detective-like figures.
Argues these detectives stayed in short anecdotes because the novel form was not part of medieval Arabic aesthetics.
athar_applications: Evidence that Arab cultural media already circulate the 'heritage detective' framing (audience familiarity); the henna-dyed hand case corresponds to HS story on al-Mu'tadid.
limitations: Journalism; unsigned; claims of 'first detective' should not be repeated as fact.

title: Dawr al-qara'in wa-l-amarat fi al-ithbat (Majallat Majma' al-Fiqh al-Islami, no. 12)
publisher: International Islamic Fiqh Academy (OIC), Jeddah - via al-Maktaba al-Shamila
key_findings: Fiqh Academy research paper (issue 12, part 12, p.1226 in the Shamela pagination) discussing stolen goods found with a suspect: Ibn Qayyim ranks this sign above testimony and confession, while Ibn Qudama treats a claim of ownership as creating doubt and Ibn Hazm rejects conviction on possession alone as judgement by conjecture.
athar_applications: Shows living Arabic juristic debate on circumstantial evidence; ATHAR can present 'possession is not proof' as an internal debate, not a Western import.
limitations: Only one page read; publication year of issue 12 not verified.
